plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Huge, softly cupped blooms rise on tall stems above round, water-beading leaves. Each flower opens at dawn and releases a sweet fragrance across still ponds.
plants.location: Temperate Asia, including the lotus ponds of Japan and China
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic waxy texture that makes water roll off and carry dirt with it. Scientists call this the 'lotus effect' and copy it in self-cleaning surfaces.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, aromatic mounds send up slender spikes of violet-blue flowers that hum with bees. Their scent drifts across summer borders and fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to August, with blooms often lasting into mid-summer
plants.location: Northern Hemisphere gardens in temperate regions, such as England and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Despite the name, English lavender comes from the western Mediterranean. Its flowers have been used for centuries to scent linens and soaps.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa
plants.description: Golden-orange flower spikes studded with wiry, hairpin-like styles glow in the winter bush. They are a feast for honeyeaters and native bees when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter and spring, roughly April to September
plants.location: Eastern Australia, from coastal heathlands and woodlands of New South Wales and Queensland to Victoria
plants.funFact: Banksias have woody seed cones that often stay closed until a bushfire passes. The heat triggers them to release their seeds onto freshly cleared, ash-enriched ground.
